description: Design a simple finite state machine (FSM) that simulates a basic SLAM process. The FSM should have three states: `Idle`, `Mapping`, and `Localizing`. The system starts in the `Idle` state. The input signal `start` transitions the FSM to the `Mapping` state. The FSM remains in `Mapping` for a fixed number of clock cycles, after which it transitions to the `Localizing` state. If the `localize_done` signal is asserted, the FSM goes back to the `Idle` state.
code:
module slam_fsm (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire start,
    input wire localize_done,
    output reg [1:0] state // 00: Idle, 01: Mapping, 10: Localizing
);

    parameter IDLE = 2'b00, MAPPING = 2'b01, LOCALIZING = 2'b10;
    reg [3:0] count; // Counter for mapping duration

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
            count <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (start) begin
                        state <= MAPPING;
                        count <= 0;
                    end
                end
                MAPPING: begin
                    count <= count + 1;
                    if (count == 4'd5) begin // Stay in mapping state for 5 clock cycles
                        state <= LOCALIZING;
                    end
                end
                LOCALIZING: begin
                    if (localize_done) begin
                        state <= IDLE;
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end

endmodule

description: Design a simple Stop-and-Wait flow control protocol in Verilog. The sender will send a data bit, and the receiver will acknowledge the received data bit. If the acknowledgment is received, the sender will send the next data bit. The sender will wait for an acknowledgment before sending the next data.
code:
module stop_and_wait (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire send_data,
    input wire recv_ack,
    output reg data_out,
    output reg ack_out
);

    reg [1:0] state; // 0: idle, 1: data sent, 2: ack received

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= 0;
            data_out <= 0;
            ack_out <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                0: begin // idle
                    if (send_data) begin
                        data_out <= 1;  // send data
                        state <= 1; // move to data sent state
                    end
                end
                1: begin // data sent
                    ack_out <= 0; // clear ack output
                    if (recv_ack) begin
                        ack_out <= 1; // acknowledge received
                        state <= 2; // move to ack received state
                    end
                end
                2: begin // ack received
                    data_out <= 0; // clear data output
                    if (!send_data) begin
                        state <= 0; // back to idle
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

    input reset,
    input actual_branch,
    input [1:0] state, // Current state (2-bits)

);
